verdict.rationale: Cloudflare Workflows, documented as part of the Workers platform, lets developers chain multiple steps, automatically retry failed tasks, and persist state for minutes, hours, or weeks with no infrastructure to manage. It can also pause for external events, and one community developer reports building a production site on Workflows. The Workers CPU-time complaint concerns plain Workers, not Workflows, so it does not contradict this capability. missing for 10: code-level documentation of the workflow definition and deploy API (how steps and retry policies are expressed in code), and independent hands-on evidence of long-running durability beyond a single anecdotal endorsement.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy durable, long-running workflows as code without manually wiring queues and retries

citations.quote: you can build applications that chain together multiple steps, automatically retry failed tasks, and persist state for minutes, hours, or even weeks - with no infrastructure to manage
Schedule cron jobs, run durable Workflows, and integrate with Queues
The ability to pause for external events or approvals
A developer said they are really enjoying Cloudflare Workflows, which they used to build mafia-arena.com.
